newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian city prepares for tropical cyclone.
newsitem.headline: Australian city prepares for tropical cyclone.

text.p: People living in the northern Australian city of Darwin were warned on Friday to prepare emergency shelters as a tropical cyclone neared the coast.
But disaster officials said the city's 75,000 residents -- many of whom still remember Darwin being devastated by a cyclone in 1974 -- did not yet need to go the shelters.

At around midday (0130 GMT) tropical cyclone Rachel was about 150 kms north-west of Darwin and heading south-west, with winds gusting at up to 120 kph (75 mph) at its centre, the Bureau of Meteorology said.
It said Rachel was not expected to make a direct hit on the city.
Police said the main road out of Darwin, the Stuart Highway, was blocked by floodwaters and advised residents trying to leave the city to return to their homes.
On Christmas Day 1974 Darwin was flattened by tropical cyclone Tracy, which killed at least 65 people.
